name: PowerSync
tagline: Sync engine that keeps on-device SQLite in sync with Postgres, MongoDB, MySQL or SQL Server.
description: PowerSync replicates data from a backend database (Postgres, MongoDB, MySQL and SQL Server) into a local SQLite database on each client, using sync rules or sync streams to decide which rows each user gets. Writes are applied locally first, queued, and uploaded through your own backend API, which keeps authorization server-side. SDKs cover Flutter, React Native, web (SQLite in WASM), Kotlin, Swift and .NET, and it can encrypt the local database. The service is source-available under FSL and can be self-hosted as the Open Edition, or used as PowerSync Cloud. It is one of the most production-ready answers to offline-first apps on an existing backend, and many former Realm users moved to it.

pricing.notes: Free cloud tier with soft limits; Team from $599/month; self-hosted Open Edition is free.

scale.notes: Service instances scale horizontally; per-client data is bounded by on-device SQLite.

strengths: Works with existing Postgres, MongoDB, MySQL and SQL Server backends
Full SQLite on the device, so local queries can use joins and indexes
Writes go through your backend API, which keeps authorization in one place
Mature SDKs for Flutter, React Native, web, Kotlin Multiplatform and Swift
Self-hostable Open Edition alongside a managed cloud
weaknesses: Service license is FSL (source-available), not OSI open source
You still write the upload handler and conflict policy on your backend
Sync rules add a second place where data access must be modelled
useCases: Flutter and React Native apps on a Postgres or MongoDB backend
Local-first web apps with SQLite in the browser
notIdealFor: Teams needing a fully OSI-licensed sync server
Apps that are always online and simple CRUD
